title: What java.lang.reflect.Proxy can and cannot do

questions.stem: Code calls Proxy.newProxyInstance(loader, new Class<?>[] {ArrayList.class}, handler). What happens?

options.text: It returns a subclass of ArrayList whose methods all call the handler.
options.says: Subclass proxies are what CGLIB or Byte Buddy generate; the JDK's Proxy never extends a class.

options.text: It returns a proxy of List, the interface that ArrayList implements.
options.says: Proxy does not pick interfaces for you; the array passed in must itself hold interfaces such as List.class.

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, since ArrayList is not an interface.
options.says: java.lang.reflect.Proxy implements interfaces only, and a concrete class in the array is refused with IllegalArgumentException.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: A proxy's handler returns a String for an interface method declared to return Integer. When does that fail?

options.text: When the method is called, with a ClassCastException at the call site.
options.says: The proxy casts the handler's result to the declared return type, so the mismatch surfaces as ClassCastException where the method was called.

options.text: When the proxy is created, with an IllegalArgumentException from newProxyInstance.
options.says: newProxyInstance never runs the handler, so it cannot know what the handler will return.

options.text: It does not fail, since the proxy converts the String with Integer.valueOf.
options.says: A proxy does no conversions beyond unboxing; a value of the wrong type is a ClassCastException.
